articles.title: La nueva realidad del baloncesto europeo: "Seis millones de cláusula es mucho, pero igual se paga"
articles.standfirst: Luis Arbalejo, director deportivo del Valencia Basket, analiza los cambios en el mercado por la llegada de nuevos ricos y la ambición de propietarios millonarios
articles.summary: Luis Arbalejo, director deportivo del Valencia Basket, analiza los cambios en el mercado por la llegada de nuevos ricos y la ambición de propietarios millonarios
articles.body: En el verano del baloncesto europeo nadie ha sufrido más las consecuencias de la nueva realidad del mercado que el Valencia Basket. El proyecto que se proclamó campeón de la Liga Endesa y alcanzó la Final Four de la Euroliga por primera vez en la historia del club se desmembró ante el pago de cláusulas de rescisión. De esa manera salieron el líder espiritual Pedro Martínez y estrellas como Jaime Pradilla (ambos con rumbo al Real Madrid por un millón de euros y 1,5 millones, respectivamente), Jean Montero (a Olympiacos por medio millón) y Brancou Badio (al Panathinaikos por 1,5 millones). Así que, intentando que no se repita algo así, el club intenta blindarse y ha establecido alguna cláusula de hasta seis millones. Otra cosa es que eso intimide a los grandes presupuestos de la Euroliga. La entrada del Dubái Basketball y el Hapoel Tel Aviv se ha unido a la ambición de propietarios con mucho dinero en los bolsillos, como los del Olympiacos y el Panathinaikos provocando una tremenda inflación. Hay clubes a los que no hay cláusulas que se les resistan y eso se asume en Valencia. "Hay cláusulas que quizás no son disuasorias para un presidente del Panathinaikos o un propietario del Hapoel Tel Aviv o el Dubái, que están pagando lo que pagan", asegura Luis Arbalejo, director deportivo de la entidad taronja. El club de los emitatos acaba de pagar 2,6 millones de dólares para sacar a Thomas Walkup del Olympiacos y, a sus 33 años y con un rol en principio secundario, le ha puesto un contrato de 9,6 millones por tres campañas. "En el baloncesto, las cláusulas, por muy altas que sean, todavía no son disuasorias. No sé hasta qué punto llegaremos. Antes, un millón era mucho y ahora mucho, quizás sean cinco o seis millones, pero es que quizá se paguen", analiza Arbalejo sobre el nuevo escenario del baloncesto europeo.

articles.title: NBA Expansion to Las Vegas, Seattle, Europe Reportedly to be Addressed by Board of Governors
articles.summary: The NBA's expansion plans may take a small step forward this week.
articles.body:
The NBA's expansion plans may take a small step forward this week.

David Aldridge and Joe Vardon of The Athletic reported the league's Board of Governors "is expected to continue to address two areas of potential expansion: the proposed NBA Europe deal and the potential domestic expansions into the Seattle and Las Vegas markets."

The board is opening its fall meeting Monday in New York City.

It's unlikely to vote on expanding into Seattle and Las Vegas, so nothing official on that front is imminent. The NBA is still weighing a number of factors including ownership candidates, basketball-related infrastructure, and the wider repercussions of adding up to two teams.

The NBA's venture into Europe is also far from his final form.

"The NBA has vetted multiple candidates for the proposed 16-team league, including 12 permanent members, with bids running from $500 million to as much as $1 billion per team, according to sources with knowledge of the discussions," per Aldridge and Vardon.

The presence of the EuroLeague is another component at play. EuroLeague owners reportedly have their own meeting scheduled in October to discuss partnering with the NBA or remaining independent and in effect being direct competition.

NBA commissioner Adam Silver has set a goal of opening play in Europe by the 2027-28 season.

If nothing else, perhaps the Board of Governors meeting will help to solidify a clearer timeline, especially as it relates to domestic expansion.

articles.title: New Celtics Rumors on 1st-Round Lottery Pick Signing Contract, Updated Roster & Depth Chart
articles.summary: Ahead of the start of NBA training camp, the Boston Celtics reportedly added some youth to their roster.
articles.body:
Ahead of the start of NBA training camp, the Boston Celtics reportedly added some youth to their roster.

Per Michael Scotto of HoopsHype, the Celtics have agreed to a deal with former Sacramento Kings guard Devin Carter, who was the No. 13 pick in the 2024 NBA draft. Carter reportedly will be competing for a roster or two-way spot in training camp.

Following the addition of Carter, Boston's updated depth chart looks like this:

After a nondescript rookie campaign, Carter appeared to still be in Sacramento's future plans when the team exercised his third-year option prior to the 2025-26 season. He played in 38 games during his sophomore campaign with 12 starts, averaging 8.9 points, 3.3 rebounds and 2.7 assists in 18.4 minutes of action. He set a career-high with 29 points on six three-pointers in a win over the Golden State Warriors in April. However, the Kings traded him to the Atlanta Hawks during the 2026 draft, and he was waived last week.

The Celtics already have a strong backcourt with two-way star point guard Derrick White and sixth man Payton Pritchard. The team also added veteran floor general Mike Conley over the offseason to provide extra depth.

Still, Boston will have to replace the production of star shooting guard Jaylen Brown after trading him to the Philadelphia 76ers. Third-year guard Baylor Scheierman is expected to take his spot in the starting lineup, though he averaged just 5.5 points across 77 games and 20 starts last season.

Carter will have the chance to prove his worth during training camp as the Celtics try to ensure they have what it takes to return to title contention during the 2026-27 campaign.

articles.title: Caitlin Clark Talks Design Process for Nike Signature Shoe in Video, Colorways Revealed in Photo
articles.summary: Less than a month out from its worldwide release, Nike pulled back the curtain on the signature shoe for Indiana Fever star Caitlin Clark.
articles.body:
Less than a month out from its worldwide release, Nike pulled back the curtain on the signature shoe for Indiana Fever star Caitlin Clark.

The company released a video Monday outlining the design process behind the Caitlin 1.

For her part, Clark wanted a shoe that would help her make quick cuts and wriggle free from defenders on the perimeter. Alex Zerzan, a product line manager for Nike Basketball, also recounted how the three-time All-Star wanted "stuff that I've never seen before."

Watch: Sophie Cunningham's viral football kick

There will be at least six different colorways for the Caitlin 1s:

For nearly 20 years, WNBA players had little to no representation within the sneaker world. That changed when Puma signed two-time MVP Breanna Stewart and gave her a signature shoe in 2022.

The Las Vegas Aces' A'ja Wilson, New York Liberty's Sabrina Ionescu and Atlanta Dream's Angel Reese have all received dedicated sneaker and apparel lines since then.

The Caitlin 1s are arguably the most anticipated of the bunch. Her fans have been eagerly awaiting the day ever since she broke through on a national stage as a junior at Iowa in 2022-23.

Beyond the design aesthetics, Nike sought to craft a shoe to Clark's specifications and on-court needs.

"The result is a signature model built around the specific demands of Clark's game, helping her play with the speed, range and unpredictability that have defined her rise, while inviting athletes everywhere to unlock new dimensions of their own game," the company said .

Clark has been wearing the shoe throughout the 2026 WNBA season. That has coincided with a strong rebound from her injury-marred 2025. She's averaging 22.5 points and 8.4 assists while setting personal highs in field-goal percentage (45.6) and three-point percentage (37.3).

The Caitlin 1s will hit stores on Oct. 1.

articles.title: 'Villain' Dillon Brooks Reveals Mike Tyson Technique He Learned and Addresses Weight Loss
articles.summary: Dillon Brooks held a basketball camp for kids and teenagers in Arizona over the weekend, and greeted them with a stare.
articles.body:
Dillon Brooks held a basketball camp for kids and teenagers in Arizona over the weekend, and greeted them with a stare.

Per Doug Haller of The Athletic, "When a slimmed-down Brooks first walked into the gym, while the 350 campers chanted his name, he stopped and stared—a breathing/focus exercise he does before games, something he took from former heavyweight champ Mike Tyson. Then he ran through the campers and gave them high fives. (Told that he looks lighter, Brooks said any weight loss was not done purposely, and he would add a few pounds now that he's back in the States. NBA training camps begin later this month. 'I feel great,' he said.)"

Brooks, 30, signed a three-year, $73 million extension with the Phoenix Suns this offseason after averaging a career-high 20.2 points per game across 56 contests. And of course, he continued to live up to his reputation as one of the NBA's most prominent pests.

"As a human being, you have good, and you have a little bit of bad, a little bit of villainy," he told Haller. "It's always in moderation, but I feel like people kind of resonate with that. A villain doesn't have to be always bad. There's good in it, as well. It's the hard work. It's the relentlessness to be the best at what you want to be, and I try to instill that in myself and try to showcase it in a different way."

articles.title: Warriors Star Steph Curry's New Disney Documentary Teased in Trailer Ahead of IMAX Release Date
articles.summary: Golden State Warriors star point guard Stephen Curry has done it all in his legendary career, and now he will be the subject of a documentary following his journey to 4,000 three-pointers.
articles.body:
Golden State Warriors star point guard Stephen Curry has done it all in his legendary career, and now he will be the subject of a documentary following his journey to 4,000 three-pointers.

Distributed by Disney, Portrait of an Artist: Stephen Curry will be released exclusively in IMAX theaters on Oct. 9, and a new trailer for the film dropped on Monday:

Curry eclipsed 4,000 career three-pointers in a win over the Sacramento Kings during the 2024-25 campaign.

"This film is all about capturing Steph Curry, an athlete and artist who is always chasing a new masterpiece," director Gotham Chopra said in a statement . "With the court as his canvas, we wanted to show the world the relentless creativity and discipline that drives one of the greatest to ever play the game. We are thrilled to be able to share this film in IMAX with audiences across the country."

Curry will enter the 2026-27 season with 4,248 career three-pointers, so it will be fun to see how high he can extend his all-time record before he hangs it up.

articles.title: Campazzo pone fecha al nuevo Real Madrid: "Ahora empieza lo bueno"
articles.standfirst: El base pide paciencia y pese a las buenas sensaciones asegura que tienen "mucho margen de mejora"
articles.summary: El base pide paciencia y pese a las buenas sensaciones asegura que tienen "mucho margen de mejora"
articles.body: Facundo Campazzo analizó el proceso de transformación del Real Madrid de Pedro Martínez. El base argentino admite que el equipo todavía está en plena adaptación a las nuevas ideas del técnico y avisa de que la mejor versión llegará con el paso del tiempo: "A medida que pasen los meses y los partidos vamos a ir mejorando". Así lo explicó en una entrevista que concedió a los medios del club blanco. Cuatro amistosos han servido para tomar contacto con el nuevo proyecto, con una derrota ante el Río Breogán y victorias frente a Baskonia, La Laguna Tenerife y Unicaja. El cambio de ritmo y la búsqueda de amenaza ofensiva desde los primeros segundos marcan la propuesta de Pedro Martínez. "Estamos viviendo ese proceso de equivocarnos mucho, pero sobre la marcha intentamos mejorar y no cometer los mismos errores", reconoce Campazzo. El margen para aprender se reduce ahora al mínimo. El viernes llega el primer gran examen con las semifinales de la Supercopa de la Euroliga ante el Dubai Basketball. El Real Madrid, subcampeón de Europa, tendrá a tiro su primer título del curso en un torneo en el que también se medirán Olympiacos y Fenerbahce. "Creo que los amistosos nos ayudaron muchísimo para medirnos y ahora empieza lo bueno, la competición", asegura el argentino. Campazzo tiene claro que el objetivo no cambia: "Es un nuevo año, con los mismos objetivos de siempre". El desafío será trasladar cuanto antes al parquet las nuevas ideas del técnico y conseguir que un equipo con varias caras nuevas alcance la velocidad de crucero. "Tenemos el primer título en unos días y es una buena prueba, con equipos de primer nivel", sentencia. Walter Tavares comparte el optimismo de su compañero. El pívot caboverdiano destaca las buenas sensaciones de un equipo que todavía tiene recorrido por delante: "Estamos teniendo muy buenas sensaciones y todavía tenemos mucho margen de mejora". Con las llegadas de Max Shulga, Timothé Luwawu-Cabarrot, Mikael Jantunen, Jaime Pradilla, Damian Jones y Olivier Sarr, además del estreno de Pedro Martínez en el banquillo, el nuevo Madrid pide tiempo para encontrar su identidad. "Creo que con el tiempo vamos a ir perfeccionando las cosas, pero vamos por muy buen camino"

articles.title: Kawhi Leonard trade to Raptors reportedly will be completed after NBA punishes Clippers for breaking salary cap rules
articles.summary: The Raptors originally agreed to a trade for Leonard in June as the Clippers did not want to sign the 35-year-old to a contract extension.
articles.body:
The previously agreed-upon trade between the Los Angeles Clippers and Toronto Raptors involving Kawhi Leonard will go through, according to ESPN's Shams Charania .

Leonard returns to Toronto, where he won the 2019 NBA championship, in exchange for 2031 and 2033 unprotected first-round selections, and a 2027 first-round swap. The Clippers also receive second-round picks in 2030 and 2033, along with forward Brandon Ingram and guard Gradey Dick .

The Clippers will still get the two first-rounders from the Raptors despite the NBA stripping the team of five first-round selections (their own picks in 2031 and 2033, along with 2029, 2030 and 2032 picks).

Losing the draft picks was part of the league's penalty for its investigation of the Clippers for allegations that Leonard received impermissible benefits, including being paid $28 million for a "no-show job," as a way of circumventing the NBA salary cap.

Ingram, 29, averaged 21.5 points, 4.8 rebounds and 3.7 assists while shooting 38% on 3-pointers after being acquired from the New Orleans Pelicans . Shortly after joining Toronto, he signed a three-year, $120 million contract extension .

Dick, who turns 23 in November, is going into his fourth NBA season. He was the Raptors' 2023 first-round pick (No. 13 overall) out of Kansas. After averaging 14.4 points and shooting 35% on 3s in his second season, Dick's scoring dropped to 6.0 points per game and 30% shooting from long range last season.

"As I return to Toronto, I am focused on what I can control, closing this chapter, and moving forward with a clean slate," Leonard said in a statement released after the NBA handed down its punishment to the Clippers.

The seven-time All-Star is expected to sign a contract extension with the Raptors, which the Clippers were not interested in doing. He is in the final year of his contract, which is set to pay him $50 million . Last season, Leonard averaged a career-high 27.9 points in 65 games with 6.4 rebounds, 3.6 assists and 1.9 steals. He shot nearly 39% on 445 3-point attempts.

Clippers, Raptors originally agreed to Leonard trade in June

The trade of Leonard to the Raptors was originally agreed upon in late June , though wasn't expected to become official until July 6 when the NBA's moratorium on transactions ended.

However, the deal was put on hold amid the NBA's investigation into the Clippers allegedly evading the league's salary cap while signing Leonard to a three-year, $103 million free-agent contract in July 2019. Both the Clippers and Raptors agreed that the trade wouldn't be completed until the league's probe was completed.

NBA commissioner Adam Silver stated during a press conference during the Las Vegas Summer League that the decision to delay the trade was not made by the league , but by the Clippers and Raptors.

NBA issues harsh penalties for Clippers avoiding salary cap rules

In addition to the Clippers being stripped of five first-round picks, team owner Steve Ballmer was fined $30 million and is suspended "from all league and team activities for one year." President of basketball operations Lawrence Frank received a six-month suspension without pay. Receiving a one-year suspension without pay was president of business operations Gillian Zucker.

Leonard himself was also fined $700,000 by the league. And Leonard's uncle and business adviser, Dennis Robertson , was also banned from engaging in any future business dealings with the NBA.

On Sunday night, Ballmer released a statement saying he accepts the NBA's punishment and won't pursue a legal challenge, as he'd previously indicated.

articles.body:
Indiana Fever star Caitlin Clark is ready for football season.

As she continues to celebrate her gold medal win in the FIBA Women's Basketball World Cup, Clark shouted out the Kansas City Chiefs ahead of their opener:

articles.title: Kawhi Leonard Traded to Raptors After Clippers Investigation, New NBA Rumors Reveal Full Details
articles.summary: The trade sending star forward Kawhi Leonard from the Los Angeles Clippers to the Toronto Raptors reportedly has officially been processed on Monday.
articles.body:
The trade sending star forward Kawhi Leonard from the Los Angeles Clippers to the Toronto Raptors reportedly has officially been processed on Monday.

ESPN's Shams Charania reported that the Clippers signed off on the trade after spending the last two weeks working through the logistics of their punishment following an NBA investigation:

Toronto obtained Leonard in a trade with Los Angeles while sending out Brandon Ingram, Gradey Dick, two first-round draft picks, two second-round selections and a pick swap on June 30.

However, the trade was put on hold while the NBA investigated Leonard and the Clippers for circumventing salary cap rules. The league eventually announced penalties for Leonard and the Clippers on Sept. 2.

Ballmer announced on Sunday night that he was accepting the league's punishment:

On June 30, ESPN's Shams Charania reported that Leonard's representatives informed interested teams on the trade market that he would only be willing to sign an extension with the Raptors and envisioned ending his career in Toronto.

The new contract doesn't come as a shock, as Charania also reported July 6 that Leonard and the Raptors were "expected to start" discussions on an extension following the trade.

The seven-time All-Star is beginning his second stint as a member of the Raptors organization, previously suiting up for them during the 2018-19 season.

Leonard exceeded expectations in his initial year on the Raptors, helping them finish with a 58-24 record before capturing their first championship in franchise history.

He averaged 30.5 points per game while connecting on 49.0 percent of his shot attempts in the playoffs with Toronto, earning Finals MVP honors after taking down the Golden State Warriors in six games.

Leonard eventually signed with the Clippers during the ensuing offseason.

The 35-year-old is coming off a dominant 2025-26 campaign in Los Angeles, averaging a career-high 27.9 points per game. He also recorded 6.4 rebounds, 3.6 assists and 1.9 steals on a nightly basis while finishing the year with 50.5/38.7/89.2 shooting splits.

Toronto compiled a 46-36 record and earned a playoff berth last season led by Scottie Barnes, who earned his second career All-Star nod and finished No. 5 in Defensive Player of the Year voting .

With Barnes and Leonard leading the way, the Raptors are expecting to contend for a championship in 2027.
